thread:
customer-john: Hey support — since yesterday ~10:30 PST some of our requests are being routed to eu-west-1 and incurring ~400-800ms extra latency. We only saw it after a spike in errors/billing credits. example curl we used: 

curl -i \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' \n  -H 'Region: us-west' \n  'https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate'

I attached request-id 01HXYZABCD and a HAR in the ticket. Can you check why region header is ignored and why EU is being chosen?

anna-support: Thanks — looking. Do you have the full request headers (redacted auth ok) and the SDK version you're using? Any proxied clients / CDN in front?

customer-john: SDK is our internal fork of redwood-js v1.2.3. Proxy is an nginx sidecar that forwards headers. Full headers (redacted):

Host: api.redwood.com
Authorization: Bearer ****
Region: us-west
X-Client-Region: 
User-Agent: our-app/4.5

note: X-Client-Region is present but empty. We didn't intentionally set it.

anna-support: aha — that empty X-Client-Region looks suspicious. Our router's header precedence used to prefer explicit headers over query/body region. I'll try to repro.

anna-support: repro steps I used locally with a tiny curl tweak:
```
curl -i -H 'Region: us-west' -H 'X-Client-Region:' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
Result: routed to eu-west and `x-routing-edge: eu-west-1` in response.

anna-support: hypothesis: the router treats presence of the header (even empty) as higher priority than the `Region` header, and an empty value is interpreted as "unknown" which triggers fallback -> EU. Not sure if fallback rule is 'unknown => nearest-pop' and that maps to eu-west for these customers. Escalating to router team. @miguel-eng-router can you confirm precedence semantics and whether empty header should be considered missing?

miguel-eng-router: thanks for the ping. Current precedence (legacy) is: 1) x-client-region header 2) Region header 3) query/body region param. We do not currently special-case empty-string. That was an assumption we never saw in prod. If a header exists but is empty we treat it as explicit "no region" and run fallback which for some customers maps to EU.

 miguel-eng-router: quick mitigation we can do: change router to ignore region headers with only whitespace or empty string and fall back to next precedence. Patch is trivial: in the header parsing path skip if value.trim().length == 0. I can cut a hotfix and a test.

jess-ml: FYI this explains why the ML latency alarms were correlated with that customer spike — the cross-region token fetches killed P95. Also watch for SDKs that set headers with empty value when serializing optional fields.

anna-support: customer confirmed their nginx sidecar sets `X-Client-Region:` when a config var is present but empty. They have a rollout that left the env var blank.

miguel-eng-router: I'll open PR, add unit + integration test against `curl -H 'X-Client-Region:'` and deploy to canary. @sre-bot please schedule a canary rollout to us-west and monitor routing metrics / p50/p95 for affected service.

sre-bot: Canary deploy request received. Will run canary on 2 nodes in us-west for 15 minutes and report routing mismatch events to #eng-sre.

customer-john: thanks team — appreciate the quick root cause and plan. Any ETA on when the hotfix will be live? Our rollout has been paused because of the extra cost.

miguel-eng-router: PR linked: https://git.internal/redwood/router/pulls/4567 — aiming for canary in 30m, full rollout in ~2h if no anomalies. We'll post updates here.

anna-support: closing loop: once patch is live we'll confirm with you that requests from your env route to us-west correctly and that billing/latency return to baseline. :thumbsup:

customer-john: confirmed after canary (checked with curl) — routing now respects `Region: us-west` even when `X-Client-Region` is blank. Thanks all.
